law: A composed method is named here by content identity and by a declared interface. Its body stays in its own SKILL.md and is never copied into this method.

Identity is the SKILL.md digest at an exact commit. A digest that no longer matches the tree means the referenced method moved, which is a re-audit, not an automatic upgrade: the interface this program relied on may or may not have survived the edit.
A declared interface states what the method takes, what it returns, and what it can never be promoted into. It is capped at 400 characters so it cannot quietly become a second copy of the procedure.
Being listed here is not admission that the referenced method is correct, current, or appropriate for a given subject. It records only that the interface was read at that digest.

composed_methods.declared_interface: in: a request whose unknowns are not enumerated. out: routed unknowns, each with an actor, a validator and a failure edge. never: a resolved unknown; routing is not an answer.
in: one research topic. out: a proposal with located sources and gate results. never: MARKET truth; a proposal is a set of located claims, not a measured arena.
in: a claim set. out: per-claim verification with an independent judge and a score. never: admission of its own verdict, and never a claim about this tree from a claim about a source.
in: one external product subject at an exact identity. out: job, pain and mechanism signals with a closure matrix. never: MARKET demand, USER validation or COMMERCIAL payment.
in: one closed subject and its claimed closure. out: read-only findings and planted-control results. never: a mutation, a repair, or admission of the findings it produced.
in: a verified corpus and a bounded question. out: a graduated minimum runtime with a stop-loss. never: USER or COMMERCIAL truth; a runtime that works is not a runtime anyone wanted.
in: one admitted program. out: an atom DAG with one owner, one lease and one writer each, plus dispatch packets. never: its own completion evidence, and never a session from a packet.
in: one atom with one writer and one declared lease. out: a stacked branch and its delivery receipt. never: the merge itself, which stays with a person.
in: two forge planes and one exact subject. out: reconciled publication state established by commit ancestry rather than by either plane's prose. never: the merge or release decision.
in: a consumer that needs a shared method. out: one shared body plus a thin binding, with same-name shadowing refused. never: evidence that the bound method executed anywhere.

not_composed.subject: any named external consumer, carrier application or runtime host
not_composed.reason: The portable core carries no consumer identity. A consumer binds this method from its own repository; naming one here would make every other consumer a special case of the first.

not_composed.subject: market, user, commercial and policy lane contracts
not_composed.reason: Separately owned by the four Stage-1 sibling lanes. They consume this contract; freezing their content here would make them children of it rather than siblings.
